Bossier City Court small claims filing deposit $65 per defendant, $20 each additional defendant

note: Fees are set court by court. Statutory base for city court small claims divisions is $35 per defendant (R.S. 13:5205) plus R.S. 13:10.3 costs, so no court actually charges just $35. sources.what: Rules of Justice Court, Rule 27(a): civil appeals from justice court are governed by Rules 5.01, 5.04, 5.07, 5.08 and 5.09 of the Uniform Civil Rules of Circuit and County Court

UCRCCC 5.01 (direct appeals from justice court are by trial de novo); 5.04 (notice of appeal and payment of costs filed with the circuit court clerk within thirty (30) days of entry of the judgment); 5.08 (supersedeas bond 125% of money judgment); 5.09 (cost bond)
DeSoto County justice court FAQ: appeals within 30 days

note: Resolved the conflict: the Mississippi Supreme Court's Rules of Justice Court (Rule 27) send civil appeals through UCRCCC 5.04, which sets 30 days, filed with the circuit court clerk with costs paid. Miss. Code s. 11-51-85 still says 10 days, but the court rules govern procedure, and DeSoto County's 30-day statement matches them. Suggested appeal text: either party may appeal to circuit court for a new trial (de novo) by filing a notice of appeal and paying costs with the circuit clerk within 30 days of judgment; collection is stayed only by a supersedeas bond of 125% of the judgment. Mention that the statute still says 10 days and to file early if unsure.

value: Either party may appeal to district court by filing a notice of appeal in the justice court within 7 calendar days from service of the judgment (JCRCP 98), with a brief statement of the basis for the appeal (JCRCP 99) and an appeal bond: a losing defendant posts the judgment plus interest, plus $100 for costs and $15 for attorney fees; a plaintiff posts $100 + $15 (JCRCP 100). Court fees also apply (e.g., Sparks Justice Court: $50 appeal fee, $115 cost bond, $211 district court fee). The district court does not hold a new trial: it decides the appeal on the justice court record and short written briefs, and you can't add documents that weren't given to the justice court (Clark County: EDCR 9.06-9.08; Washoe County: WDCR 19(4)).
